card.name: Verb or comma after a long subject
card.fires_on: The word "could" after a long subject ("risk ... beyond 24 weeks could not be assessed"), and commas that open an "if" clause after "completely" or "three months and".

modes.label: could not be assessed
modes.description: The word "could" right after a long subject, before "not be assessed".
modes.example: the risk of suicidal thoughts or behavior beyond 24 weeks<< could>> not be assessed.

modes.label: Comma before an if-clause
modes.description: A comma that interrupts a sentence just before a conditional "if" clause.
modes.example: the syndrome may remit, partially or completely<<,>> if antipsychotic treatment is withdrawn

card.writes: It suppresses "could" and similar words, and weakly promotes words like "often", so it seems to discourage another "could" at that spot.
card.plain: It fires on "could" or on a comma that sits in the middle of a long label sentence, just before the sentence's condition or main verb.
